description: Ancient societies used open-pit mining and quarrying to extract stone and mineral deposits that lay close to the surface. Workers removed soil and overburden, then cut into exposed rock using picks, hammers, chisels, wedges, and sometimes fire-setting to loosen harder material. These pits supplied building stone such as limestone, sandstone, marble, and granite, as well as ores and decorative minerals. The extracted material could then be shaped on site or transported to workshops, construction projects, temples, fortifications, roads, and monuments.
